I love this game!  It's cozy, lowkey, allows you to take things at your own pace, and a good amount of challenging.  Dying in the dungeon causes you to lose a majority of your inventory, but the dungeons are simple enough that it doesn't feel too punishing.  If you're good at video games, you can go through the dungeons without much worry for upgrades, but if you're like me and kind of suck at combat, you can also grind for bit and get weapons that make the dungeons much easier.  I think the mechanics are fun, the graphics really cute, and I haven't had any bugs or glitches so far.  

The ONLY thing I don't like, and I actually really really hate this thing, is the wanderer.  This big green monster that appears if you take too long in the dungeon.  It's unkillable, gives no drops, and chases you throughout the entire dungeon level, including during combat.  I just died halfway through a dungeon, losing a full inventory, because it's impossible to do a boss fight when an immortal blob that can kill you with one hit is chasing you around a very limited arena space at the same time.  All for the crime of being thorough.  It genuinely sucks, makes the game less fun, and serves no point.  

Other than that, though, I really do enjoy the game, and I fully intend to play it to completion.

I will not recommend this game because it has it's qualities, it has a nice concept and it was made with love but I had higher expectations. A lot of reviews sum up my toughts but, nonetheless, I'm going to expose them (was playing on the hardest difficulty):

The artwork is, indeed, amazing. The movement seems fluid, the attacks and interactions as well as the monster behaviour is something pleasant to see. BUT...

It is a great set of gameplay ideas put together but done superficially in every way. It is shallow.
The shopkeeping idea seems awesome at first. You sell your itens according to a specif demand for them and adjust the price to the reactions that the npcs show to your item's prices. That's the main concept. But in practice:

Regarding your Shop:
- The customers only have 4 reactions to your pricing and it gets monotonous later on. There is no depth to the shopkeeping management;
- They will almost always buy your itens as long as it's not really overpriced;
- There is a small thief minigame that has no creativity and, after a few times you feel like it is only wasting your time;
- The customers also, later in the game, ask for tasks that can be summed up to "kill and/or fetch" quests; 
- There are upgrades you can make to your shop but you can make money so fast that they don't really feel like a challange.
- There are separeted contents you can buy from another shopkeeper in town that can upgrade your customer's reaction. Like statues, tapestry, flowers. Decorations to your shop. But after you buy them they do not appear anywhere. It's frustrating. 

Regarding the exploration parts:
- There is an ok variety of weapon, but, again, no depth involved. You can only follow two lines of upgrades for each weapon: an elemental one and a non-elemental one.
- Same pattern go for the armors. There are tree types of armor. One that gives more HP and reduces movement. A balanced one that gives moderate amount of both and a third one that gives less HP and increases a lot your speed. And that is it.
- There is a simples potion crafting shop as well.
- As stated above, it is so easy to make money that you can just spam your way into potions and clear all the dungeons.



TL;DR:

- It is a beautiful game but shallow in every aspect.
- Three main concepts put together: a story, a shopkeeping mechanic and a dungeon exploration one. But every one of them lacks in depth.
- The game is literally what you see in the trailers. There is almost nothing left to uncover or to be surprised at.
- I'm writing this review more because I felt disappointed than because it's a bad game, cause it is not. I just expected way more.

It feels like the game's potention was somehow, should I sum up the review, wasted.

Cheers,

I don´t know how to feel about Moonlighter. The main gameplay loop consists of going into a dungeon where you kill monsters and progress further. After you complete the dungeon or escape, you will try to sell all the stuff that you gathered in your little shop. On paper it sounds fun, but I found some things in this game that just made me upset.

The first problem I had with this game was the combat. I thing that the movement and actions that the character does are extremely slow and not really fluent. It feels like there is very big cooldown after attack co you can´t roll immediately. I understand why the devs did it, because then the game would be much easier. But for me it ruined the thrill of battling in the dungeon. Later in the game I found my self just rushing through the floors, so I can get to the boss. Because that was the only intense moment in the dungeon. Everything in the dungeon is a little slower than I would want. Sometimes even the boss wasn´t any challenge because of the speed of the game.

The second problem was the progression system. Only way to progress in this game is by grinding the materials in the dungeons and then selling them so you can upgrade. Yeah what else should I expect from this game right? But I feel like that this would not be such a problem if the dungeons were more fun.

Also the story is nothing special and the dialogs are not interesting.

I really like the shop management part. The selling system is very fun and complex. For every item that you have you decide what it will cost and you hope that you guessed the right price. When someone wants to buy it, they make expression if they like the price and how much they like it or not. Based on that you try to modify the price so that its worth it for you and for the customers. Because if you sell overpriced stuff then no one will buy from you. Sometimes you can up the price a little bit on item that has a high demand and you will get away with it. However if the customers start to hate your price on some items, then you need to lower the price a lot or put it on big sale. This way running the shop every day makes it an enjoying and very interactive experience that I was always looking forward to.

As for the graphics and overall style of the game. I feel like its alright. The pixel art is pleasant to look at and the soundtrack is sometimes good and sometimes not so much. I haven't found anything to hate but also to love about it.

My conclusion is. If you are looking for a game that is grindy, slow, not so challenging and has fun shop management mechanics. Then this game is for you. But I was not able to stick to this game till the end because of it. Maybe one day I will come back to this game and finish what I started but who knows.

Sadly, I can't recomend this game. I wish I could, since it has really cool ideas and great art, but it fails in everything else.

I'll explain briefly how this game works. You are a merchant in a small town. And you need things to sell. So you enter a series of dungeons to slain enemies, open chests and loot everything you can to sell in your little shop. The game cicle is simple, first you enter the dungeon, then you manage your store. Rinse and repeat.

And that sounds really cool. Except every single mechanic involved is as shallow as it can be. Let's begin with the dungeon side. It's design resembles a roguelite. You enter a series of procedural dungeons to get items. You get those items back. You repeat over and over again. And that sounds cool right? Roguelites are awesome (one of my favourite genres). Except in Moonlighter you have to do this without all the variety you find in a roguelite. You only have five different weapons (four melee ones that just change the combo and a bow), and the only thing you do with those weapons is repeat the same 3-hit combo over and over again (think of 2D Zelda games combat). That's like playing The Binding of Isaac but only having the basic tears, or Dead Cells only with the initial equipment. If you have to repeat the same dungeon over and over again with a ton of different options, it's cool. But if you have to do so with 2D Zelda style of combat, it gets boring. Really quick. 

Then you have your store. At first it sounds cool, managing the items you put up for sale and deciding the price they are gonna sell for. This, just like the combat, gets boring really quick. Once you find out an item's optimal price, it's just a repetitive task you have to do every time you exit a dungeon.

The story happens to suffer the same fate, being too simple to be enjoyable.

I hate to do this. I really do. Moonlighter has really cool ideas. But it also gets boring after just a couple of hours.
